item.title: Advertising banners, posters and abandoned signs: A435/Finlay Way, Bishop’s Cleeve, 17th August
item.description:
Unauthorised? Advertising banners, posters and abandoned signs, A435/Finlay Way, Bishop’s Cleeve There appears to be an increasing number of advertising banners and posters being attached to roadside fencing, posts and barriers around the roundabout on the A435 heading towards Finlay Way in Bishop’s Cleeve, and then being left behind once the event has finished or a property has been sold. Alongside the abandoned roadwork signs that are also being left in the area, this is becoming not only increasingly unsightly but potentially a safety concern. As the weather changes, unsecured banners and signs may become loose and could potentially be blown into the road, creating a hazard for motorists and potentially causing an accident. The attached photograph shows a “SOLD” estate agent sign which has been left attached to the roadside fencing, along with various other banners. These signs create visual clutter and, with this becoming increasingly common, I am concerned that the problem will continue to worsen. Please could this be investigated and, where appropriate, the responsible companies be asked to remove their banners and posters once they are no longer required? It would also be helpful if the Council could clarify whether there is any enforcement action available to prevent businesses from repeatedly putting up advertising material and then leaving it behind.

Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): Bishop's Cleeve, Tewkesbury

item.title: Tree blocking access to my drive, 16th August
item.description:
I am writing to formally request urgent action regarding the council-owned tree located at the entrance to my driveway at 84 Reddings Road, Cheltenham. Over recent years, the tree has grown significantly, and its expanding root system is now actively lifting the tarmac surrounding its base. This ground displacement has created a severe vehicle clearance issue and a structural hazard at the sole point of access to my property. The physical restriction is now critical. When my neighbor has a vehicle parked on their adjacent driveway, maneuvering around the raised tarmac and tree trunk is exceptionally difficult. Continued root growth will very shortly render my driveway entirely inaccessible by car. Furthermore, the uneven, buckling tarmac poses an immediate trip hazard and risks causing damage to vehicles. Given that the tree is severely compromising safe, unhindered vehicular access to my private residence, I request that an officer inspect the site as a matter of priority to determine an appropriate solution—such as root management, resurfacing, or removal. I have attached a photograph clearly showing the extent of the tarmac displacement and the resulting access obstruction. I look forward to hearing from you regarding a date for an inspection.
